decisions.executionNote: Layout is reversed from reference: prepare right arm to hold the holder, leaving left for pens. Begin gradual elbow-up reorientation with small increments.
Advance right gripper toward the holder from its right side, gradually completing horizontal inward orientation; left remains clear.
Replan after rejected yaw step: hold current orientation, shift inward and forward with smaller translations to avoid the discontinuous IK branch.
Lift open fingers above the holder rim before moving forward, avoiding a lateral collision with the near finger.
Center right open fingers around holder and lower to its sidewalls, then close. Verify holder retention in the next view.
Keep right gripper closed and test retention by a slow upward, inward lift; prior lowering showed significant contact/tracking error.
Holder did not visibly lift. Reopen and reposition forward and lower around its walls before another grasp; use small translations.
Lower fingers farther onto holder sidewalls, close fully, then make a small retention-test lift.
Wrist view shows holder offset toward the far side rather than centered. Reopen and shift forward/inward to put it between the jaws.
Lower onto the holder body with open jaws, then close and pause. Link6 is above the intended sidewall grasp; visual retention remains uncertain.
Contact prevented descent. Lift and reopen, then move slightly outward and rearward to center the holder between the jaws rather than under one fingertip; reduce tilt.
Use wrist view: holder remains to the far side of the jaws. Shift the open right gripper forward and a little inward while clear of the rim, then descend cautiously.
Rejected prefix moved nothing. Begin with a smaller lift and slight orientation bridge to satisfy continuity, then reposition the open jaws toward the holder.
Bridge the opposite small wrist-rotation direction after another zero-step rejection, then lift and shift open fingers toward the far side of the holder.
Holder is now closer to wrist-image center. Lower the open gripper to the body and make a final small forward alignment, watching for contact.
Holder is centered between the open jaws in wrist view. Lower another 3 cm onto its sidewalls, close fully, and make a small test lift.
Close command remains zero. Lift the holder and bring it toward the center-right transfer area; verify that it follows the wrist.
Holder follows the right wrist. Move it to the center-right loading position while beginning a gradual downward-facing approach with the left arm.
Hold the holder steady and move the left gripper above the black pen, rotating toward a top-down grasp while preserving the current elbow-up branch.
Approach the black pen from above, completing the downward orientation and shifting toward its barrel. Holder stays closed and stationary.
Shift the left grasp toward the upper barrel, close fully, and begin a small retention-test lift while holding the holder steady.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table and begin rotating the retained black pen upright; keep the right-held holder stable.
Black pen is visibly retained. Raise it above the holder rim while completing the upright orientation and moving toward the center without crossing arms.
Align the upright black pen over the holder opening from the left; keep its tip above the rim until centered.
Visual alignment shows the pen tip right of the opening. Correct leftward and lower slowly toward the rim, keeping both grasps closed.
Tip is visibly inside the opening. Lower the black pen farther, release it into the held holder, then withdraw upward slightly.
Black pen remains in the holder. Withdraw the open left hand safely and begin reorienting for the white pen next.
Move above the white pen and progressively rotate the open left gripper downward, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Complete top-down alignment with the white pen and descend to a pregrasp height; the holder remains stationary in the right hand.
Descend around the white pen's upper barrel with open jaws, correcting along its slanted axis before closing.
Center the white barrel between the fingers, lower slightly, close fully and lift to verify retention.
White pen is visibly retained. Lift away from the table and rotate it toward upright while retracting to a comfortable elbow-up configuration.
Complete the white pen's upright rotation and raise its tip above the holder rim, approaching the unoccupied left part of the opening.
Move the white tip rightward off the rim and lower it slowly into the free part of the opening. Keep the pen held until insertion is visible.
White tip is visibly within the opening. Lower farther, release it beside the black pen, then lift the empty left gripper.
Two pens are visibly in the held holder. Withdraw the open left hand and start a downward approach for the cyan marker.
Continue orienting the left fingers downward and approach above the cyan marker; maintain the right holder grasp.
Finish downward alignment and descend to a safe pregrasp height over the cyan marker, keeping the holder stable.
Descend open fingers around the cyan marker's upper body, advancing along its axis and correcting its slight image slant before closing.
Cyan marker is centered. Lower to the body, close fully, and lift vertically to check retention before rotating.
Cyan marker follows the closed fingers. Lift and retract it clear of the tabletop, rotating gradually upright on the same elbow-up branch.
Raise the cyan marker above the holder and complete its upright orientation before final visual alignment.
Align the cyan marker's lower end over the free left side of the opening and lower toward the rim, retaining it until insertion is visible.
Nudge the cyan marker away from the left/far rim and lower slowly into the opening, monitoring possible rim contact.
Cyan lower end is within the opening but contacting other contents. Release without further pushing and lift the empty hand clear so the holder can settle.
Move toward the remaining purple marker and rotate for its diagonal tabletop axis. Cyan remains supported at the opening but its final seating is uncertain; inspect again after settling.
Complete the downward grasp orientation above the purple marker and descend toward pregrasp height, keeping the right-held contents stationary.
Descend toward the purple marker's upper body with open fingers, advancing along its diagonal axis and correcting the remaining image slant.
Purple marker is centered between the open fingers. Lower slightly, close fully, and lift vertically to verify retention.
Purple marker follows the left fingers. Lift well clear of the table and rotate toward upright before approaching the holder.
Complete upright purple orientation and raise its long lower end above the rim before shifting over the opening.
Shift the purple marker off the left rim toward the remaining opening, then lower slightly to check clearance among the other pens.
Purple is above the leaning cyan marker rather than free space. Shift toward the front of the opening, then test a small descent without releasing.
Purple is contacting the black pen cap. Lift slightly, offset toward the gap beside it, and retry a short descent without forcing the contents.
Purple lower end projects within the opening. Try a slow 4.5 cm insertion with a small offset away from the black cap, retaining the marker until seating is visible.
Purple lower end is in the holder region. Release it and withdraw without further pressure, then inspect whether all four settle before returning the holder to the table.
All four pens appear supported by the holder. Begin returning the left hand while carrying the holder forward/down and gently correcting its rightward lean before placement.
Holder now appears upright at the tabletop. Lower slightly to support its base, open the right hand and ease away while continuing the left hand's return.
Purple fell onto the table during placement; three pens remain. Regrasp the upright holder with the right hand and redirect the left hand toward the fallen marker without crossing arms.
Lower the reopened right jaws below the rim for a sidewall grasp. Continue left approach above the fallen purple marker, keeping the left wrist on its side of center.
Recenter right jaws forward around the holder rather than a rim/pen contact. Approach the purple marker with a slight inward fingertip tilt while keeping the left wrist left of center.
Fine-center the left fingers around the purple body, close and test-lift. Recenter the open right jaws slightly rearward before a cautious descent around the holder.
Test retention of the purple marker with a clear lift. Lower right fingers onto the holder sidewalls, close fully, and make a small test lift.
Purple did not lift. Reopen and approach it about 2 cm lower with the same inward fingertip tilt. Test the right holder grasp by raising it clear of the table.
Center the purple barrel in the wrist view, close at the lower grasp height, and test retention with a vertical lift. Right holder now follows the hand.
Purple is now visibly retained. Lift it well clear and retract the left wrist while rotating toward upright; keep the loaded holder steady.
Finish upright rotation of the retained purple marker and approach above the holder without descending among the other pens yet.
Purple is right of the opening. Shift it left and slightly forward above the gap, keeping it held and avoiding the right gripper body.
Lower purple toward the opening with a small offset toward the gap beside cyan. Keep it gripped until the lower body is clearly below the rim.
Avoid landing on the white pen by lifting slightly and shifting purple toward the farther free portion of the holder opening before deeper insertion.
Lower purple slowly toward the aligned opening, retaining it throughout; stop to inspect depth and any rim or pen contact before releasing.
Purple is resting on the cyan cap, not inserted. Lift clear and shift toward the visible free slot beside cyan before another careful descent.
Adjust purple toward the small open region beside the other pens, then test only a short descent while keeping it gripped.
Head view places purple's lower end on the right edge. Lift clear, offset left and slightly toward the front slot, then lower a short distance to inspect clearance.
Purple is still perched on cyan. Lift and move toward the far-side empty slot, using the right wrist view to clear the cyan cap, then test lowering.
Purple now clears cyan and is above the far-side gap. Move slightly inward from the rim and lower slowly into that slot, keeping it held.
